data.body:
Premise confirmed empirically from live Reconcile Bridge logs (GitHub Actions).

Four consecutive live passes (runs 31568815075, 31569179421, 31569723185, 31570037358, spanning ~30 min on 2026-08-12) each emit exactly 19 failed inbound link writes: 5 'source ticket is closed', 13 'redundant link — ancestor-descendant relationship', 1 'would create a cycle at epic level'. Normalising the log lines and diffing two of those passes yields a BYTE-IDENTICAL failing set — same source, same target, same relation, same reason. So the reconciler has no memory of the outcome: it re-derives and re-attempts the identical impossible set every pass.

The failing call site is named in every line: rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records::_apply_inbound_update — it invokes 'rebar link', catches RebarError, logs WARNING, and continues. That warn-and-continue is the whole of the current handling.

Quantified waste: 19 doomed link writes per pass, passes run continuously (~every 5-6 min), i.e. roughly 200+ known-doomed writes per hour, indefinitely, plus 19 permanent WARNING lines forming the error floor described in the ticket.
